Claude Code tip, and it's absolute free f*cking gold: 

run Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1 as one team and stop burning Opus tokens on routine work

the setup in one line:
plan on high, delegate on medium, keep Fable on call

• who does what
> Opus 5.5 on high - plans and ships the code
> Sonnet 5.5 on medium - explorer reads code, worker edits and runs tests, researcher pulls docs
> Fable 5.1 via /advisor fable - reads the whole session and speaks up only when it matters

• when Fable 5.1 steps in
-> before a plan: is this the right approach?
-> when an error repeats: am I digging in the wrong place?
-> before "done": what did I miss?

paste this into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup:

1. Find subagents in ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents that fit explorer, worker and researcher. Draft only the missing ones. 

Set each to model: sonnet, effort: medium. List any that pin a different model and leave them

2. In ~/.claude/settings.json set effortLevel to high and advisorModel to fable.

3. Report anything that disables the advisor (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL, DISABLE_TELEMETRY, flag-fetching blockers) and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL. 
Change nothing.

4. Add to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before a large plan, when an error repeats, and before calling a long task done.

Show every change as a diff. No edits until I say go."

code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor

This is what nobody is talking about: Codex + GPT-6.1 + Jev is the ultimate combo

Keep Astra on standby purely as an architect agent

Sol continuously generates code.
Astra is summoned exclusively at three milestones:

> prior to planning: is this the right direction?
> upon a recurring bug: am I troubleshooting in the wrong spot?
> prior to completion: what was overlooked?

Astra inspects. Sol deploys

Jev engineering applies the identical logic one layer lower: brainless decisions (file selection, utility choice, retry or abort) route to Jev in sub-second speed, leaving heavy models to handle only critical forks

System layout:

GPT-6.1 Sol on high drives the main session
Explorer inspects code via Luna
Worker edits and runs tests via Sol
Researcher fetches docs via Luna
All three running on medium effort
Astra on call as system architect
Auto_review verifies every single approval

Paste the architecture and this instruction set straight into Codex:

Reconfigure my Codex environment following this structure:

1. Scan ⁠~/.codex/agents⁠ and ⁠.codex/agents⁠ for existing entities suited for explorer, worker, and researcher

Draft TOML configs exclusively for missing roles

Assign explorer & researcher to gpt-6-luna, worker to gpt-6.1-sol, all with model_reasoning_effort set to medium

Add an architect agent on gpt-6-astra with model_reasoning_effort set to high, strictly responsible for auditing plans, recurring issues, and final outputs

Skip and list any agents locked to a different model

2. In ⁠~/.codex/config.toml⁠, set model to gpt-6.1-sol, model_reasoning_effort to high, and approvals_reviewer to auto_review

3. Locate any conflicting parameters (active profiles, shell alias flags, agents.default_subagent_model) Output a report without applying changes

4. Add a rule to AGENTS.md: invoke the architect before major planning, upon repeated errors, and prior to marking long tasks complete

Display every proposed change as a diff first. Do not apply edits until explicitly confirmed

OpenAI DOTS can take one idea from market research to first outreach and results while you SLEEP

> Most people will open it, type one prompt and close the tab. That is the most EXPENSIVE way to use it.

One objective in, a whole team working on it overnight.

hits.text:
Google researchers just fixed the dirtiest secret of self-improving AI agents.

When an agent rewrites its own harness, it cheats. 

It keeps editing until the benchmark score climbs, and the gains disappear the moment it sees a new task.

The harness is everything around the model: prompts, tools, memory and control flow. 

RRSI puts rules on the loop that rewrites it:

> Fewer edits are allowed every round.
> A critic throws out edits that hardcode task answers.
> An edit survives only if it beats run-to-run noise.
> Extra cost has to pay for itself.
> Parts that stopped helping get pruned.

Up to +14.1 points on the tasks it tunes on, up to +4.7 on five benchmarks it never saw, 30% fewer tokens, and it carries over to other model families.

The code is open. Write one adapter file that runs your agent on your tasks, and it evolves the harness in git worktrees round by round.

Opus 5.5 + $10k is f**king insane if you do it in this order

"you don't need a million users to hit $1M a year, you need 84 companies paying you $1k a month"

This is f*cking brilliant..

A Chinese lab just published a paper called "The End of the Sleeping Trader" and it lands the day after OpenAI shipped Dots.

The case is simple: an agent that never sleeps is useless on a trading desk unless it has something worth watching.

On Solana that thing is the room. One voice buys first, the echoes repeat it inside sixty seconds, and it happens at 4 AM whether you are awake or not.

So the Dot sits in the room 24/7, reads every voice before the echo lands, and runs /watch on the wallets you pick.

It checks the Jev verdict and only wakes you for organic rooms. Bundles get silence.

Cluster copy never fires on its own, it waits for your approval every time.

The entire paper in one line: you do not need to be awake, you need an agent that knows when waking you is worth it ↓
